And all default subverses should be required to have a public moderation log enabled.
Moderators should have the ability to enable a public moderation log.

I agree entirely. Transparency with regards to moderation is essential to establishing some amount of trust between readers and moderators.

The issue with personal information and illegal content being shown on a log is a legitimate concern, and there needs to be a way to flag a thread as within one of those parameters so that the title would be visible, but not the content.
Also a toggle to remove the username, as it could become a public board of shame then.

I don't understand the need for that. Why not publicly shame people who are spamming, or gaming or posting illegal content. That way other users can see who is to be trusted or not.

Or do you mean don't display the mod's user name in the log?

Perhaps what could be displayed is the title of the submission, the domain name, and the username of the mod who made the removal. The log wouldn't include the link itself so that the content, if illegal, would no longer be directly linked within the website.

Eh, having the username of the mod itself isn't a great idea. This leads to doxing attempts from users, and a large separation between users and moderators. I would also add a way for the moderator to put a removal reason for the public to see.

I get that it's not fun to have a witch hunt coming for you, but including the username of the moderator making the removal would tend to make mods more selective in what they remove which, I think, is a good thing.

In any event, I agree that it would be good for moderators to have a place to note the reason for the removal in the public moderation log.
All moderation logs should be public imo...
The only backlash to this that I could think of is if it shows a mod that deletes a discussions/links and comments this can cause witchhunting on those mods.
I like the compromise of not having it automatically visible which moderator deleted something.

I don't see the point if you don't know which mod. Just defeats the purpose. How about the moderator, the comment, username blank. We could tell when a mod was abusing power, without causing witch hunts for the user...? Any opinion?

That wouldn't really be any different from just displaying all the information, since anyone angry about their stuff being removed can just say "This is mine!" So far I've been open with what I've deleted in /v/science, and no one has gone after me with scary Internet hacking. I'm in favour of the compromise because if there ever is a larger conflict, the community can point to what's been done and either the mods can have a talk about it without people knowing whom in particular to mess with, or Atko can step in, have a closer look at who's been doing what, and decide whether to kick someone/replace the mod team.
